## Threads that kept coming back

- **The sea dream** first appears as calm water and dry feet [2014-06-15], then becomes a slow, literal progression: one toe [2015-12-14], both feet [2018-12-29], floating [2020-09-21], swimming [2022-01-02], and finally teaching someone to float [2026-02-03]. The loop closes when Vó Lúcia appears young and laughing in the dream [2026-07-20].
- **Limonada** begins as three lemon seeds in a yogurt cup [2016-01-12], becomes a named plant [2016-11-30], and stays alive for years without producing lemons [2016-12-30], [2020-12-30], [2025-12-20]. The promise to keep it “forever” is still being kept.
- **Drawing** starts as “one page a week” [2014-01-30], disappears and returns as “small is still drawing” [2015-06-15], and later becomes half your income [2025-12-20]. Vó Lúcia’s hands recur from memory, wrong and right at once [2017-01-05], [2024-07-03].
- **Tio Beto and “Asa Branca”** is a promise repeated across years [2014-10-26], [2014-11-24], [2016-12-18], [2020-05-11], [2022-12-29], [2026-10-15]. The loop closes when you play it without sheet music and laugh at your own mistake [2026-10-15].
- **Vó Lúcia** moves from Sunday calls and jabuticaba [2014-09-20] to grief [2020-10-30], then to drawings of her stories and hands [2016-10-18], [2024-07-03], [2026-10-02].

## What you let go of

- **Rafa** mattered intensely [2015-02-23], then became a playlist, a pastel, and a small warmth rather than a wound [2021-11-20], [2022-03-26], [2026-10-28].
- **The factory** was once feared as “forever” [2021-03-12], then left behind [2023-12-01], [2023-02-03].
- **The república fridge** and its yogurt names were a small daily comedy [2014-07-19], [2015-01-09], [2021-02-20], and eventually became memory rather than life.

## Promises to yourself

- **Pass Cálculo** [2014-01-30]: still open; no later capsule says.
- **Draw one page a week** [2014-01-30]: kept, unevenly and repeatedly [2016-12-30], [2023-10-01], [2025-12-20].
- **Call Vó every Sunday** [2014-01-30]: kept while she was alive [2015-12-27]; changed by loss [2020-10-30].
- **Learn to swim** [2014-01-30], [2024-01-12]: kept, not gracefully [2024-07-03], [2025-12-20].
- **Plant lemon seeds** [2015-02-28], [2016-01-12]: kept; Limonada survived [2025-12-20], but producing lemons remains still open.
- **Draw for a living / live near the sea** [2021-05-30], [2021-09-05]: changed into half-income illustration and not-yet-own-window [2025-12-20].
- **Vó’s book** [2022-12-27]: still open, though her hands are “right on page seven” [2025-12-20].

## A letter from all your past selves

You kept more than you think. You did not become fearless, but you became less afraid of the water, and that was the whole point. You kept drawing when no one asked, kept calling, kept planting, kept practicing the same song badly and lovingly. You lost Vó, lost Rafa, lost the factory, and did not lose yourself. You are still the girl with seeds in a napkin, just with better hands. Keep going. [2014-01-30], [2020-10-30], [2026-10-15]

## Threads that kept coming back

- **The sea dream.** First written down [2014-06-15] as sitting on sand with someone unseen, feet dry. It recurred for over a decade, each version a small step forward: one toe in [2015-12-14], both feet [2018-03-25], floating [2020-09-21], swimming [2022-01-02], and finally teaching someone to float [2026-02-03] and swimming beside a young, laughing Vó Lúcia [2026-07-20]. The dream closed its own loop.
- **Limonada, the lemon tree.** Seeds kept in a napkin [2014-12-08], planted in a yogurt cup marked "MARINA" [2016-01-12], given a note in her pot [2018-11-11], sketched in her own tiny book [2020-03-21], replanted again [2024-03-10], and still alive and shedding flowers at ten years old [2025-10-05], [2026-10-02]. The question "did anything ever come of that?" got its answer: yes, a whole relationship.
- **"Asa Branca" and Tio Beto.** Promised [2014-10-26], re-promised [2014-11-24], practiced through the second verse [2016-12-18], played all the way through [2023-12-28], and finally played without sheet music [2026-10-15]. Tio Beto's voice note with mistakes in the same places [2026-11-30] closed the loop: the inheritance was never the song, it was the stubbornness.
- **Vó Lúcia's hands.** Drawn on a napkin at Mom's [2016-07-03], redrawn from memory [2017-01-05], [2020-10-30], [2024-07-03], and finally "right on page seven" [2025-12-20]. She died [2020-10-30]; the drawing kept her.
- **Seu Ivo and Juca the parrot.** A bus comic [2016-12-30], an Interbairros printout found years later [2022-06-01], a stranger with a green parrot on the street [2023-04-15], a comic again [2023-10-01], and Tio Beto hearing a parrot on the radio [2025-06-28]. The first thing that felt like yours never stopped being yours.
- **The fridge with names on yogurts.** [2014-07-19], [2015-01-09], [2016-01-12], remembered with longing [2021-02-20]. A small, ridiculous city that became a whole era.

## What you let go of

- **Rafa and São Paulo.** From "I like him, I don't know if I like São Paulo" [2015-02-23] to a breakup [2018-03-25], to not sending the dog-in-sunglasses photo [2019-02-02], to listening to his playlist "not for him, just for the songs" [2021-10-25], to thinking of him for one second and the pastel for thirty [2026-10-28]. The playlist stayed in a folder called "não apagar" [2021-11-20] but you stopped pressing play.
- **The factory.** Named as a fear [2021-03-12], [2021-03-18], then gone: "first December without the factory" [2023-12-01].
- **The "two years then the sea" timeline.** It took longer than two years [2025-12-07]. You arrived anyway.

## Promises to yourself

- **Pass Cálculo** [2014-01-30]: never mentioned again. Still open.
- **Draw one page a week** [2014-01-30]: kept, lapsed, restarted [2023-10-01], and by 2025 half your income is illustration [2025-12-20]. Kept.
- **Call Vó every Sunday** [2014-01-30]: kept [2015-12-27] until she died [2020-10-30]. Kept, then ended by loss.
- **Learn to swim** [2014-01-30], [2024-03-10]: kept. "Not well. But the promise is kept" [2024-03-10].
- **Plant lemon seeds** [2014-12-08], [2015-02-28], [2016-01-12]: kept. Limonada is ten [2025-10-05].
- **Live near the sea / own window facing sea** [2021-05-30], [2025-12-20]: still open. "Not from my own window yet. Working on it."
- **Vó Lúcia's book** [2022-12-27]: still open. "Vó's book doesn't yet" [2022-12-27]; "don't rush the book" [2025-12-30].
- **Play "Asa Branca"** [2014-10-26]: kept, imperfectly [2026-10-15].

## A letter from all your past selves

You kept asking us the same questions — did the lemon tree make it, did you learn to swim, did you keep drawing — and we are tired of asking, so here is the answer: yes, yes, and yes, messily and constantly. You were scared at 20 and scared at 27 and scared at 30, and you drew anyway, which was the whole point. You never got the sea window, not yet, but you stood in the water up to your ankles and called it a start, and then you swam, and then you taught someone else to float. Vó Lúcia is gone and her hands are still right on page seven. Tio Beto is still waiting and you are still playing, wrong in the same places. We are proud of you, and we are also still a little afraid. That's fine. Keep drawing. [2014-01-30], [2024-03-10], [2026-10-02]

## Threads that kept coming back

- **The sea dream** first appears as calm water and dry feet [2014-06-15], becomes a toe in the water [2015-12-14], both feet [2018-12-29], floating [2020-09-21], and finally swimming with Vó Lúcia [2026-07-20]. It tracks your fear and your courage more faithfully than any diary entry.
- **Lemon seeds and Limonada** begin with seeds kept in a napkin [2014-12-08], become a yogurt-cup plant named MARINA [2016-01-12], and stay alive for years [2020-03-21], [2025-12-07]. The tree never becomes the dramatic lemon tree you asked about, but it becomes a companion.
- **Drawing** starts as “one page a week” [2014-01-30], disappears and returns as one small fish [2015-06-15], becomes Vó’s stories [2016-10-18], and eventually becomes half your income [2025-12-07].
- **Vó Lúcia** appears through calls and the jabuticabeira [2014-09-20], then through memory, hands, and grief [2020-10-30], [2026-10-02]. Her hands remain a recurring subject [2024-07-03].
- **Tio Beto and “Asa Branca”** run from 2014 [2014-10-26] through repeated “one more year” promises [2014-11-24], [2020-05-11], to playing without sheet music [2026-10-15].
- **Rafa** moves from crush [2015-02-23] to breakup aftermath [2019-02-02], then to a softer memory [2021-11-20], [2026-10-28].
- **Bia** stays present through bus rides [2015-12-27], voice notes [2020-11-19], and later daily life [2025-02-08].

## What you let go of

- The **república fridge** and its yogurt names [2014-07-19], [2015-01-09] fade into nostalgia [2021-02-20].
- The **factory** shifts from fear [2021-03-12] to something you leave behind [2023-12-01].
- **Rafa’s playlist** moves from active ache [2018-11-25] to a folder you do not open [2021-11-20].
- **Vó Lúcia’s voice** is lost, but her hands and stories remain [2020-10-30], [2026-10-02].

## Promises to yourself

- **Pass Cálculo** [2014-01-30]: still open; no later capsule confirms it.
- **Draw one page a week** [2014-01-30]: kept, unevenly, and returned to [2016-12-30], [2023-10-01].
- **Call Vó every Sunday** [2014-01-30]: kept while she lived [2015-12-27], then changed by loss [2020-10-30].
- **Learn to swim** [2014-12-27], [2024-03-10]: kept [2024-05-30], [2025-12-07].
- **Plant lemon seeds** [2014-12-08], [2015-02-28], [2016-01-12]: kept in the form of Limonada [2020-03-21], [2025-12-07].
- **Draw for a living** [2021-05-30], [2021-09-05]: half-kept [2025-12-07].
- **Live near the sea / own window** [2021-05-30], [2022-06-03]: still open [2025-12-07].
- **Vó’s book** [2022-12-27]: still open [2025-12-07].
- **“Asa Branca”** [2014-10-26], [2014-11-24]: changed from promise to ongoing practice [2026-10-15].

## A letter from all your past selves

You kept drawing when no one asked. You called Vó on Sundays until you couldn’t. You planted seeds in a yogurt cup and kept the plant alive longer than you kept most plans. You were afraid of the water, then you put a toe in, then both feet, then you swam. You did not become fearless; you became less afraid, which is better. You still forget verses, still draw parrots, still talk to plants. We are proud of the mess. Keep going. [2014-01-30], [2020-10-30], [2026-07-20]

## Threads that kept coming back

- **The sea dream** first appears as standing at the edge with stuck feet [2014-05-11], then slowly changes: one toe in [2015-12-14], feet wet [2016-07-23], floating [2020-09-21], swimming [2023-03-12], and finally Vó Lúcia swimming beside you [2026-07-20].
- **Vó Lúcia** appears as Sunday calls and the farm in Irati [2014-03-10], becomes “menina do mar” [2018-10-29], and after her death her hands and stories keep returning in drawings [2020-10-30, 2026-04-22].
- **Tio Beto and “Asa Branca”** begin as three chords [2014-04-12], become the running “one more year” joke [2014-11-02], and finally reach the end of the song [2026-07-28].
- **Limonada** starts as lemon seeds in a yogurt cup [2016-01-12], becomes a stubborn, leafy, mostly fruitless companion [2021-10-14], and finally produces a real bud [2024-12-22].
- **The parrot man / Seu Ivo and Juca** first appear in the Álgebra notebook [2014-04-14], return in bus comics [2016-12-30], and still surface years later [2023-04-02, 2025-06-02].
- **Bia** is there from the friendship bracelet [2014-02-03], through the república roof and satellites [2014-06-11], to Floripa voice notes and the sea outside her window [2020-05-16, 2022-11-26].

## What you let go of

- **Rafa** mattered deeply [2015-02-23], but later the playlist becomes something you can hear without making it a wound [2021-10-25, 2024-09-22].
- **The factory** was once “fine” but not enough [2022-12-18], and you eventually leave it [2023-01-08].
- **The old fear of being seen as “not normal”** softens; Mom’s “good” becomes a word you keep [2019-12-12, 2022-08-06].
- **The idea that drawing must be hidden** moves from under the mattress to the desk and then into public work [2016-07-12, 2018-03-04, 2025-10-20].

## Promises to yourself

- **Keep drawing one page a week** [2014-03-10]: kept, messily and constantly [2016-12-30, 2025-12-21].
- **Learn to swim** [2014-03-10]: kept, not gracefully but truly [2024-04-10, 2025-10-05].
- **Call Vó Lúcia every Sunday** [2014-03-10]: kept while she was alive [2015-12-27]; after her death it becomes memory and drawing [2020-10-30, 2026-04-22].
- **Play “Asa Branca”** [2014-11-02]: kept, eventually, with the same stubborn mistake [2026-07-28].
- **Plant lemon seeds / keep a lemon tree** [2016-01-12]: kept; Limonada survives and finally buds [2024-12-22].
- **Live near the sea / draw for a living** [2021-05-30]: partly kept; illustration becomes half your income, and the sea is close but not yet from your own window [2025-12-21].
- **Publish the book** [2020-10-10]: still open, though you are circling yes [2026-09-30].

## A letter from all your past selves

You kept the small things: the seeds, the bracelet, the parrot, the song, the Sunday calls. You did not become fearless; you became less afraid of the water. You drew when no one asked, swam when no one watched, and let Vó Lúcia’s hands stay alive on the page. You left the factory, kept Bia, kept Tio Beto’s “one more year,” and finally played the song through. The sea is no longer only a dream. We are proud of you, especially for the ordinary days. [2014-03-10, 2024-04-10, 2026-07-28]

## Threads that kept coming back

- **Drawing** first appears as a 2014 promise to yourself: “keep drawing, at least one page a week” [2014-03-10]. It wobbles—failed Cálculo, two months without drawing [2014-03-16], sketchbook hidden under the mattress [2015-08-10]—but it never fully leaves. By 2016 you can say “I drew every week. Promise kept” [2016-12-30], and by 2025 illustration is half your income [2025-10-20].
- **The sea dream** starts as stuck feet and tight calves [2014-05-11], [2014-05-26]. Over years it changes: one toe in [2015-12-14], both feet [2018-05-03], floating [2020-09-21], swimming [2023-03-12], and finally swimming with Vó Lúcia laughing beside you [2026-07-20].
- **Vó Lúcia** is there from the first Sunday calls [2014-01-30], [2014-03-10]. Her farm, Coronel, the jabuticabeira, and her hands become the book you are still making [2020-10-25], [2026-04-22]. Her death in 2020 [2020-10-30] does not end the thread; it changes it into memory and drawing.
- **Tio Beto and “Asa Branca”** is a running joke that becomes real practice: “one more year” [2014-11-02], [2016-04-02], [2018-10-28]. By 2026 you get through the second verse without stopping [2026-07-28], and later play without sheet music [2026-10-15].
- **Bia** appears in the friendship bracelet [2014-02-03], the roof and satellites [2014-06-11], Floripa windows [2020-05-16], and voice notes [2022-11-26]. She stays the first person you text [2024-09-20].
- **Limonada** begins as three lemon seeds in a yogurt cup [2016-01-12]. For years she has leaves but no lemons [2018-11-04], [2021-02-19]. By 2024 she has a real bud [2024-12-22], and by 2026 one remaining lemon on New Year’s [2026-12-31].
- **Rafa and the playlist** move from crush [2015-02-23] to breakup [2018-02-19] to something softer: you can listen without crying, or cry a little and still call it progress [2022-12-18], [2024-09-22].
- **The parrot man / Seu Ivo / Juca** keeps returning from the margins of notebooks [2014-04-14], [2017-08-01], [2023-10-01], [2025-06-02]. He is one of the first things that felt like yours.

## What you let go of

- **The factory as identity.** You stayed long enough to know it was not forever [2018-11-25], then quit in 2023 [2023-01-08], [2023-01-26].
- **The idea that drawing had to be hidden.** The sketchbook moves from under the mattress to the desk [2016-07-03], [2016-07-12], [2018-03-04], and eventually becomes work [2025-10-20].
- **Some versions of “one more year.”** Not all of them disappear, but they stop being only postponement and become practice [2022-07-29], [2026-07-28].
- **The old fear of the water.** It does not vanish in one moment; it thins out across years of small swims [2021-07-02], [2024-05-30], [2026-02-03].

## Promises to yourself

- **Pass Cálculo / survive engineering:** broken at first [2014-03-16], later kept in part—Cálculo 2 passed [2016-11-03]. Engineering itself becomes a detour, not a life [2023-03-08].
- **Draw one page a week:** kept, messily and constantly [2016-12-30], [2025-12-21].
- **Call Vó Lúcia every Sunday:** kept while she was alive [2015-12-27], [2020-09-19]; after her death, the Sunday still catches you [2025-03-01].
- **Learn to swim:** kept. Not gracefully, but truly [2024-04-10], [2024-05-30], [2026-02-03].
- **Plant lemon seeds / keep a lemon tree:** kept. Limonada survives moves, cold, and panic [2021-02-19], [2023-10-05], [2026-12-31].
- **Finish Vó’s book:** still open, but actively alive [2020-10-25], [2026-07-20], [2026-09-30].
- **Live near the sea / see it from your window:** kept by 2024 [2024-09-20], [2025-12-28].
- **Play “Asa Branca” all the way through:** kept in 2026, imperfectly [2026-07-28], [2026-10-15].

## A letter from all your past selves

You kept drawing. You learned to swim. You did not become fearless, but you became less afraid, and that was enough. Vó Lúcia is gone, but her hands are still on the page. Tio Beto is still waiting for the next verse. Bia is still the first person you text. Limonada finally made a lemon. You quit the factory, moved toward the sea, and did not stop being yourself. We are proud of you, even the versions of you who hid the sketchbook under the mattress. Keep going. [2014-03-10], [2020-10-30], [2026-12-31]

## Threads that kept coming back

- **Drawing as the through-line.** It starts as a 2014 promise to draw one page a week [2014-01-30], gets buried under engineering and Mom’s “hobby, not a job” [2014-03-10], then keeps resurfacing: bus comics, Vó’s hands, the sea, motors, Vó’s stories [2016-07-03, 2021-10-24, 2025-12-28]. By 2025, half your income is illustration [2025-10-20].
- **The sea dream.** From 2014, it is always the same edge, warm water, stuck feet [2014-05-11, 2014-12-12]. It changes slowly: one toe [2015-12-14], sitting instead of fighting [2015-01-30], floating [2020-09-21], swimming [2023-03-12], and finally Vó Lúcia swimming beside you [2026-07-20].
- **Vó Lúcia.** She is the Sunday call, the farm, Coronel, the jabuticabeira, and the phrase “menina do mar” [2014-03-10, 2018-10-29, 2020-10-30]. After her death, she becomes the book and the drawings of her hands [2020-10-25, 2024-04-28].
- **Tio Beto and “Asa Branca.”** The promise repeats for years: “one more year” [2014-11-02, 2016-10-17, 2018-10-28]. The loop closes when you play it through, imperfectly, and laugh [2026-07-28, 2026-10-15].
- **Bia.** From friendship bracelets and açaí fights [2014-02-03, 2014-02-05] to voice notes, windows, and the sea [2020-05-16, 2022-11-26, 2024-09-20]. She stays the first person you text [2024-09-20].
- **Limonada.** Planted from lemon seeds in 2016 [2016-01-12], she becomes a running companion: leaves, flowers, no lemons, then a bud [2022-11-05, 2024-12-22].
- **The parrot man / Seu Ivo / Juca.** A small 2014 image keeps returning in drawings and memory [2014-07-14, 2023-04-02, 2025-06-02].

## What you let go of

- **Rafa.** The relationship fades from daily presence to playlist, then to a one-second thought before the pastel [2015-02-23, 2018-02-19, 2026-10-28].
- **The factory identity.** You leave it in 2023 and stop measuring vibrations for a living [2023-01-08].
- **The república era.** The yogurt fridge, the bus, the 7am calculus become memory rather than daily life [2014-07-19, 2021-02-20].
- **The old fear of being “ungrateful” for leaving engineering.** It loosens through therapy and the solar startup [2021-08-01, 2023-01-08].

## Promises to yourself

- **Draw one page a week:** kept, messily and constantly [2014-01-30, 2016-12-30, 2025-12-21].
- **Learn to swim:** kept by 2024, not gracefully but truly [2014-03-10, 2024-04-10, 2024-05-30].
- **Call Vó Lúcia every Sunday:** kept while she lived; broken by loss, not neglect [2014-03-10, 2020-10-30].
- **Keep drawing despite Mom’s doubt:** kept, and eventually acknowledged by her [2015-08-10, 2022-08-06, 2024-11-03].
- **Play “Asa Branca”:** kept, late and imperfect [2014-11-02, 2026-07-28].
- **Publish the book / Vó’s stories:** still open; the publisher email is there, but the yes is still being sat with [2020-10-25, 2026-09-30].
- **Live by the sea:** kept, though not from your own window yet [2021-05-30, 2024-09-20, 2025-12-21].

## A letter from all your past selves

Dear you,

We were scared, and we kept writing anyway. We missed Sundays, failed calculus, hid sketchbooks under mattresses, and still drew one fish, one hand, one wave. We promised swimming, drawing, calling Vó, playing “Asa Branca,” and we meant all of them, even when we were late.

We did not become fearless. We became less afraid of the water, less afraid of saying the true thing, less afraid of being seen. You still talk to plants, still draw on receipts, still miss Vó. That is not failure. That is loyalty.

Keep the window, the book, the sea, and Bia’s voice notes. Keep the imperfect song. We are proud of you, and we are still here in the margins.

Love,  
all of us [2014-01-30, 2020-10-30, 2026-12-31]

## Threads that kept coming back

- **Umbrellas and rain:** from the first capsule, rain and forgotten umbrellas are a running joke [2014-01-05], [2014-01-07], [2017-02-26]. The loop never fully closes; it becomes part of your Curitiba identity rather than a problem to solve.
- **The sea dream:** the same dream appears for years—warm water, feet that won’t move [2014-07-02], [2015-09-22], [2020-09-28]. It slowly changes: one step, then a hand, then no panic. The fear doesn’t vanish; it becomes smaller and more livable.
- **Vó Lúcia:** she moves from phone calls and bolo de fubá [2014-01-30], [2014-08-02] to stories about Coronel and the jabuticabeira [2014-11-24], [2015-04-18], then to drawings of her hands and kitchen [2016-12-26], [2018-02-25], [2019-12-22]. She becomes a quiet center of gravity.
- **Drawing as promise:** “draw one page a week” [2014-01-30] becomes a self-imposed discipline [2016-12-18], then a career thread [2016-05-18], [2023-03-25], [2026-03-15]. The promise is kept, but in fragments: lunch breaks, margins, bus rides.
- **Limonada:** the lemon tree becomes a small living companion [2016-11-26], [2019-03-26], [2025-02-23]. You panic over leaves, move her, wipe dust, and eventually let her be imperfect [2020-02-29], [2026-12-30].
- **Seu Ivo and the parrot:** first seen on the bus [2014-08-02], later drawn from memory [2023-11-12], [2023-11-19]. He becomes a symbol of ordinary reliability.
- **Bia and the sea window:** from república fridge names [2014-02-03] to Florianópolis and the spare room facing the sea [2018-01-09], [2019-08-01], [2022-08-24]. The wish becomes real, then ordinary, which is better.

## What you let go of

- **Rafa:** the breakup is still present in 2019 [2019-02-02], but by 2023 the pastel memory has no sadness [2023-05-28]. You let go without erasing him.
- **The factory forever fear:** named in therapy [2021-03-18], then slowly replaced by movement, savings, and a sea fund [2023-09-03], [2023-11-19].
- **The need to prove:** swimming shifts from “I can’t” [2016-11-11] to “I’m just swimming” [2023-08-12]. The performance drops away.
- **Some drawings:** you stop posting everything [2018-11-18], [2023-11-19]. Privacy becomes a form of maturity.

## Promises to yourself

- **Call Vó every Sunday:** missed immediately [2014-01-30], but the relationship deepens anyway [2014-08-02], [2019-12-22].

## A letter from all your past selves

Dear Marina,

We kept the umbrella question open on purpose. You still forget, and it still rains, and somehow that became a kind of home.

We are proud of the small things: the page a week, the 25 meters, the lemon tree that survived your panic. We are also proud that you stopped needing every small thing to mean something.

You did not become fearless. You became someone who can stand at the edge and take one step. That was enough for us, and it is enough now.

Keep drawing the hands. Keep calling Vó. Keep writing names on things, even when no one asks.

Love,  
all of us [2014-01-05], [2016-12-18], [2023-08-12], [2026-12-30]

## Threads that kept coming back

- **The sea, and the dream of not being able to enter it.** It first appears as a childhood dream in [2014-07-02], returns in [2015-09-22], [2019-08-25], [2020-02-28], and [2020-09-28], where your feet finally move one step. By [2023-08-12] you swim 25 meters alone, and by [2025-10-05] you can list “swimming: yes” among the things 18-year-old you wanted.
- **Vó Lúcia, Coronel, and the jabuticabeira.** Vó appears early in [2014-07-16], Coronel and the tree in [2014-11-24] and [2015-04-18], and the story keeps returning through drawings, calls, and family meals, including [2019-12-22] and [2022-06-15].
- **Drawing as the constant.** From the condensation self-portrait in [2014-01-05] to the weekly sketchbook promise in [2016-12-18], the Interbairros strips in [2016-05-18], and the sea drawings in [2025-12-21], drawing is the thread you keep choosing.
- **Buses, Curitiba, and small public scenes.** The parrot man appears in [2014-08-02], returns in memory in [2020-05-19] and [2023-11-12], and the bus itself stays a place where you notice people, including [2026-08-22].
- **Limonada.** The lemon tree appears in [2016-11-26], drops leaves in [2018-11-04] and [2022-02-07], gets dusted in [2021-01-08], and is still there, with a small lemon, in [2026-12-30].

## What you let go of

- **The factory as a permanent identity.** In [2018-12-20] you say “two years, Marina”; by [2021-03-18] you write “the factory forever” as a fear, and by [2023-08-12] you are swimming without proving anything.
- **Rafa as an open wound.** The breakup is still raw in [2019-02-02], but by [2023-05-28] the pastel place brings “no sadness, just the taste of mint tea after.”
- **The need to be brave in a dramatic way.** In [2013? no] [2014-12-15] you imagine a window with the sea; by [2022-08-24] you simply stand at Bia’s window, and she photographs your back.

## A letter from all your past selves

Dear Marina,

We kept the umbrella question open, but we kept the drawing. We forgot words, missed Sundays, burnt rice, and still showed up. We were scared of the sea, then one step, then twenty-five meters. ## A letter from all your past selves

Dear you,

We wrote you from buses, from the república fridge, from the edge of a sea we couldn't enter. We were eighteen and scared and already imagining a window with the sea in it [2014-12-15]. ## A letter from all your past selves

Dear you,

We wrote this in pieces, across twelve years, on buses and kitchen tables and the edge of a sea we couldn't enter. We were scared and hopeful and broke and stubborn, and we kept drawing anyway, even when it had to hide under a mattress or in the margins of an Álgebra notebook.

We want you to know: the lemon tree made a fruit. You learned to swim. You sent the book. Bia is still the first person you text. Vó Lúcia's hands are in your lines now, and Mom prints your comics without saying she likes them, which means she does.

We also want you to know we were tired, and we kept going, and that was enough. You don't have to be brave every day. You just have to keep showing up with a pen.

The sea is still there. So are you. That was always the point.

— all of us, 2014 to 2026

## A letter from all your past selves

Dear Marina,

We were cold, broke, and stubborn, and we kept drawing anyway. We forgot umbrellas, failed matrices, burned rice, and stood with our feet in the water because that was as far as we could go. We were scared of the sea, of money, of being ordinary, of leaving the factory, of showing the drawings. We kept the lemon seeds, the yogurt cup, the parrot, the sock, the postcard. We called Vó, missed her, and drew her hands until they became a language. We did not become fearless. We became someone who swims a little farther, eats the dry cake, and lets the lemon stay on the branch. We are proud of you, and we are still here in the margins.

Love, all of us.

## A letter from all your past selves

Dear Marina,

We were cold, broke, late, and drawing on fogged windows. We forgot umbrellas and matrices and rice. We kept the sketchbook under the mattress and the sea above the bed. We were scared of water and of being ordinary, and we wrote it down anyway.

You did not become fearless. You became someone who goes in anyway, one step, then two, then twenty-five meters. You kept Bia, the parrot, the bus, the lemon tree, and Vó’s hands. You let Rafa become a taste instead of a wound. You let the factory become a chapter, not a sentence.

We are proud of the small things: the pastel, the float, the page one, the lemon that finally came. We are also proud that you still draw parrots in margins.

Keep the tree alive. Keep the sea in the room. Keep saying things out loud.

— all of us, from 2014 to now
